call_points.text: India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for the rest of FY27 on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline assortment changes.
Of the 280 bps gross-margin loss in Q4, only 20 bps recovered in Q1; full recovery seen by Q3-Q4.
Crude-linked and rupee-depreciation cost increases to be fully passed on to customers by end of Q2.
About 100 net store additions planned this fiscal, with FY28 expansion to be better.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 on the width-to-depth assortment change.
International adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to 7% of revenue from 10%; no breakeven date given.
GlobalBees revenue was flat on a planned brand warehouse transition, expected to complete in Q2 with growth back from Q3.
Pre-school segment revenue rose 47% to ₹19 Cr and adjusted EBITDA 65% to ₹5 Cr; target is 1,000 preschools in a couple of years.
Analyst pressed on international breakeven timing; management declined to give a quarter, saying only "sooner than you think".
Analyst asked for the profitability gap between diapering and non-diapering; management gave no number, only that diapering is not loss-making.
International adjusted EBITDA losses fell 33% YoY in Q4FY26 and 35% in FY26.
Two horizontal e-commerce players that entered UAE and KSA in 2024 keep promotional activity elevated.
Globalbees core categories grew 28% in FY26 with ₹92 Cr adjusted EBITDA post corporate expenses.
India multichannel was PAT and free cash flow positive in FY26; consolidated free cash flow was also positive.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune dated January 30, 2026, under the Income-Tax Act, 1961, wherein an addition of Rs. 93,57,99,520/- has been made to the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 w.r.t Transfer Pricing adjustment of Rs. 10,84,95,240/- and addition on account of disallowance of ESOP expenses: Rs. 82,73,04,280/-, and consequently a tax demand of Rs. 31,36,30,330/- has been raised.In continuation to Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune, Company made an application to the Authority and on verification of the case records by the said Authority, the Company is in receipt of the rectification order and demand notice from the Authority wherein the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 is now recomputed as Rs. 52,54,110/-, thereby reducing the amount of demand for AY 2022-23 from Rs. 31,36,30,330/- to Rs. 38,37,210/- (i.e. by Rs. 30,97,93,120/-).
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax Department Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal with Hon. ITAT on 26th March 2026.

penalties.details: The Court issued an order imposing a penalty of Rs. 25,000/-
penalties.impact: The Company has paid the penalty amount of Rs. 25,000 on 28.04.2026 and the matter stands closed.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Office of the Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication), Mumbai, via order dated January 13, 2026, had demanded a differential duty along with redemption fine and penalty on the Company amounting to Rs. 6,56,58,134/- (exclusive of applicable interest under Section 28AA of the Customs Act, 1962), ("Order") primarily on interpretational grounds in respect of alleged violation in connection with failure to comply with procedural aspects of documentation relating to country of origin of the imported goods, under Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA) framework.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of the Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal against the said order before the Customs Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) on April 11, 2026.

guidance.statement: India multi-channel growth rate to remain elevated in subsequent quarters of FY27
Crude-linked and rupee-depreciation cost increases fully passed on to customers
About 100 net store additions this fiscal year
1,000 preschools over the next couple of years

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Services > Retailing > E-Retail/ E-Commerce

operating_notes.text: FY26 exceptional items (net) of ₹50.01 Cr included ₹35.57 Cr of non-recoverability of current assets including inventories at Globalbees step-down subsidiaries and ₹14.52 Cr impact on retirement benefits including the new labour code.
Diapering is about 15% of India multi-channel GMV; non-diapering is 85%, with fashion over 50% of GMV and home brands over 50% of business.
RocketBees covers 72 cities and more than 50% of online volumes with 20% better delivery turnaround; FC Qwik did 1,25,000 shipments in 12 cities in June, up from 60,000 in five cities in March.
Pre-school segment has 500-plus preschools under FirstCry Intellitots on a royalty model.
NCLT New Delhi rejected and dismissed Section 7 IBC application filed by Ashutosh Garg, Paritosh Garg and Manju Agarwal against Globalbees Brands for ₹64.92 Cr.

Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,162.67 Cr, net loss to shareholders ₹30.31 Cr (against a loss of ₹76.74 Cr a year earlier).
